Application Materials.content:
- Transcript: “We will need a transcript (in English or a certified translation) giving full details of subjects studied and grades/marks obtained.” Send scanned or certified copies of transcripts and **not** the originals.
- One completed reference: Applicants should check whether one or two references are required for the programme. “You should supply at least one reference from an academic referee who is in a position to comment on the standard of your academic work and suitability for postgraduate level study.” References from other sources, such as an employer or colleague, may be accepted where an academic reference is not possible; references from family members, partners or spouses are not accepted.
- Reference submission/format: References can be uploaded via the online application system, via the Gateway after submission, posted, sent via the [enquiry form](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/enquiry/), or emailed by the referee from a university or company email address. References for postgraduate applications must be in **pdf format, on headed paper, dated, signed/stamped and recommend you for your chosen programme**. If sent direct by the referee, it should come from their institutional or company email address and can be sent to [pg-ad@exeter.ac.uk](mailto:pg-ad@exeter.ac.uk), along with the student reference number, name and programme of study.
- Personal statement: “not all programmes require one,” but applicants may provide one. It should be tailored to the course and include how the course links past and future, insight into abilities and fit with the course, evidence of skills/commitment/enthusiasm, reasons for wanting to study at the University of Exeter, and particular interest in the subject. Keep it **under 500 words**, use short and clear sentences, consider headings, proofread, and use a standard font such as Arial or Times New Roman, text size 11.
- Essential documentation for an initial decision on taught programme applications: applicants should send as many required supporting documents as possible with the application; as a **minimum**, complete the Module Information section with details of outstanding modules and expected completion date, and send any interim transcripts available to support the application.
- International students: original copies are not required at the application stage and are not recommended during the application process. If academic or English language qualifications are not yet completed, an offer may normally be made conditional on completing these and supplying any required references; documentary evidence must be provided before the offer can be considered unconditional.

Interview Requirements.content: Pre-CAS Interview: We may require you to attend an interview before we issue you with your CAS. If you are required to attend an interview, we will send you an email with details of the time and date and joining instructions. The meeting will take place via Microsoft Teams. The purpose of the Pre-CAS interview is to assess that an applicant has a genuine intent to study at the University of Exeter, it is not to assess academic abilities. Attendance at an interview is mandatory and we will be unable to issue a CAS until the interview has taken place. Applicants required to attend a Pre-CAS interview will be sent further details once they have an unconditional place and where applicable a deposit has been paid.

Application Deadlines.content:
Teaching starts for most programmes in **late September**.
For **international applicants** wishing to join in 2026/2027, the application deadline is **23:59 Friday 11 September 2026** UK time.
International applicants are advised to submit a complete application by **mid-July** for September start.

Academic Requirements.content:
- **A 2:2 or equivalent** from a recognised university, including **at least one mathematical / quantitative module at 2:2 or equivalent**.
- The University will consider applications where there is evidence of exceptional performance in modules relevant to the programme of study, **significant relevant work experience or professional qualifications**.
- For applicants from China: applicants to Exeter master's programmes need a bachelor's degree certificate and graduation certificate from a domestic university recognised by the Chinese Ministry of Education, with grades equivalent to UK 2:1 or 2:2; different programmes have different grade requirements.
- For China postgraduate taught entry standards in 2026: **2:2 = 70%** and **2:1 = 75%**.
- For China: the previous domestic university ranking requirement has been removed; all Chinese universities are assessed using a unified score standard, and all undergraduate institutions on the official recognised list of the Chinese Ministry of Education are accepted. Some courses may have additional undergraduate subject-background requirements.

Program Overview.content:
MSc Business Analytics is a **1 year full time** programme at **Streatham Campus**, with September-to-September or January-to-January start options depending on the chosen start month. The programme is for students interested in a career related to business analytics or wishing to study a related PhD, and teaches students how to support managers to make data driven decisions using techniques including optimisation and forecasting, analysis of data from social media and marketing, and approaches connected to environmental and global business challenges.
The programme provides foundations in business analytics, basic programming and mathematical skills, plus techniques to present and communicate data to managers. Students can flex the programme through optional areas such as Marketing Analytics, Strategic & HR Analytics, Operations Analytics, and Environmental Analytics. The programme is delivered over three terms and is University-based throughout; taught components are delivered in the first two terms, with the third term used to complete a Business Project based around a sizeable business problem and supervised by an academic from the Business and Management department.
The University of Exeter Business School is triple accredited by **AMBA, AACSB, EQUIS**. In the QS Business Master’s Rankings 2025 for Business Analytics, the programme is ranked **26th globally** for diversity and **top 90 globally** for employability. High achieving students may apply for the Quantitative Techniques for Economics and Management (QTEM) programme, which includes an additional semester at one of QTEM’s academic partners, a quantitatively focused internship, and participation in the QTEM Data Challenge.
Teaching is delivered through lectures, workshops, practical sessions, practitioner insight seminars, private study, case study development, group work, individual projects, and collaboration with industry partners. Students benefit from the University of Exeter Business School teaching environment and support resources, including the [Centre for Innovation in Business Education](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/research/centres/teaching/). The University has invested **£50 million** in Data Science and Artificial Intelligence capabilities through the Accelerating Data Science and Artificial Intelligence (ADA) project, which benefits the programme.
Students are taught by internationally respected academics active in the University of Exeter Business School’s research culture. The programme is embedded within the [Operations and Analytics group](https://business-school.exeter.ac.uk/management/about/operations-analytics/) in the Department of Management, and the [Centre for Simulation and Analytics Management](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/research/centres/csam/) supports research and teaching in the programme, focusing on analytical modelling and computer simulation to address real-world problems including circular economy modelling, resilience to climate change, and urgent medical and emergency care.
Graduates develop the ability to use data and analytics confidently and creatively to resolve operational and strategic problems across sectors. After graduation, students join more than 26,000 Business School alumni in over 150 countries. Graduate roles include Business Consultant, Data Consultant, Business Analyst, Supply Chain Analyst, Marketing Analyst, HR Analyst, and Business Manager, with opportunities in consulting, tech, finance, procurement, HR, marketing, public and third sector organisations, and Graduate Management schemes.

Curriculum.content:
Duration: **1 year full time**. Entry year: **2026 + January 2027 start**. Campus: **Streatham Campus**.
The programme is delivered over **three terms** and is **University-based throughout this time**. The taught components are delivered in the first two terms, leaving the third term to complete the Business Project. The programme runs from **September to September** or **January to January** depending on chosen start month.
During the programme students study modules totalling **180 credits**: **120 credits of compulsory modules** and **60 credits of optional modules**. Students complete a research project / Business Project supervised by an academic from the Business and Management department, based around a sizeable business problem that draws upon business analytics skills.
Compulsory modules:
| Code | Module | Credits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BEMM457 | Topics in Business Analytics | 15 |
| BEMM458 | Programming for Business Analytics | 15 |
| BEMM459 | Database Technologies for Business Analytics | 15 |
| BEMM460 | Statistics and Mathematics for Business Analytics | 15 |
| BEMM461 | Analytics and Visualisation for Managers and Consultants | 15 |
| BEMM828 | MSc Project | 45 |
Optional modules:
| Code | Module | Credits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BEMM394 | Entrepreneurship: New Venture Creation | 15 |
| BEMM462 | Operations Analytics | 15 |
| BEMM463 | Marketing Analytics | 15 |
| BEMM464 | Strategic and HR Analytics | 15 |
| BEMM465 | Environmental Analytics | 15 |
| BEMM783 | Supply Chain Analytics | 15 |
| COM2019 | Programming for Prompt Engineering | 15 |
| SSIM916 | Machine Learning for Social Data Science | 15 |
The programme includes core modules in business analytics, basic programming and mathematical skills, and techniques to present and communicate data to managers. Optional modules allow students to flex the programme to suit interests and career or research aspirations, including areas such as Marketing Analytics, Strategic & HR Analytics, Operations Analytics, and Environmental Analytics.
Teaching is delivered through lectures, workshops, practical sessions, practitioner insight seminars, private study, case study development, group work, individual projects, and collaboration with industry partners. Assessment includes practical exercises, project work, written assignments, presentations, multiple-choice tests, and examinations.
High achieving students enrolled in MSc Business Analytics may apply for the [QTEM Programme](https://business-school.exeter.ac.uk/study/studyabroad/pgstudyabroad/qtem/). If accepted, students spend an additional semester studying at one of the academic partners, followed by a quantitatively focussed internship and participation in the [QTEM Data Challenge](https://www.qtem.org/en/students/data-challenge/1), which includes online data science and leadership courses as well as real data analysis.

Cost of Attendance.content:
For international students, the University estimates a single student living in Exeter or Cornwall will need approximately **£1,300-£2,000 a month** to meet basic living expenses such as accommodation (rent), transport, food and drink, entertainment, utility bills, clothes and socialising.
| Expense | Average cost per week* |
| --- | --- |
| Student halls (bills included) | £150-£270 (self-catered); £250-£345 (catered) |
| Rooms in private accommodation (without bills) | £135-£250 |
| Household bills (gas, electricity, water, broadband & a TV licence) | £30 |
| Groceries | £60 |
| Socialising (dining out, going to cafes & bars) | £40 |
| Public transport | £18 |
| Mobile phone bill (SIM only plan) | £4.50 |
| Student gym membership | £15 |
| **Total** | **£316 - £421/week estimate** |
*Based on average local spend April 2026.
As an approximate estimate for a single person living in shared accommodation, household bills per month are: gas £55 - £75, electricity £65-£85, internet £25 - £35, water £30-£40. A TV Licence costs £13.25 per month.

Financial Aid.content:
Exeter Excellence Scholarships 2026/27 - Postgraduate Taught (Masters), Round 4 - January 2027 entry only: Awards of **£3,000, £5,000 or £10,000** are available, and **MSc Business Analytics** is one of the eligible campus-based Masters programmes.
You can apply if you:
- have International fee status, including any EU applicants required to pay International fees in 2026/27;
- already hold an offer, conditional or unconditional, to study an eligible Postgraduate taught degree at the University of Exeter, beginning in **January 2027**;
- have not applied in Round 1 or 2 of the 2026/27 Exeter Excellence scholarship scheme for September 2026 entry for the same programme.
Scholarship recipients are selected on academic merit and the ability to demonstrate academic and career ambitions, a clear plan for making the most of the study opportunity, and a sense of social responsibility and willingness to engage with the Exeter community. Applicants will typically be expected to demonstrate that they have achieved or are able to achieve the equivalent of UK upper second class degree (2:1).
To be considered, once you have your programme offer, apply using the webform [here](https://forms.cloud.microsoft/e/4vjgYKQZb1). A personal statement of no more than 300 words is required.
**Round 4 - January 2027 entry only closes on Thursday 26 November 2026. Round 4 notifications will be sent out within one month on a rolling basis and no later than Thursday 10 December 2026.**
These scholarships are awarded as a reduction in the first-year International tuition fees. They are not recurrent for subsequent years of study. They can be combined with a University of Exeter Postgraduate Taught Scholarship 2026/27 for Bangladesh, Canada, China (mainland), India, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Nepal, Pakistan, South Korea, Sri Lanka, Taiwan, Thailand, Türkiye or Vietnam to a maximum award value of **£10,000**.
| Application deadline | Value | Duration of award | Contact |
|---|---|---|---|
| **26th November 2026** | **£3,000, £5,000 or £10,000 first year tuition fees discount** | for 1 year | Admissions Scholarships: [admissions-scholarships@exeter.ac.uk](mailto:admissions-scholarships@exeter.ac.uk) |

Multiple Applications.content: No. When you accept your place on a programme you are committing to that specific programme. Any other offers you may be holding will be released.

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
Requests for deferral will be considered on a case by case basis. Applicants wishing to defer will need to put their request in writing and [submit it via our enquiry form](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/enquiry/) (please ensure you quote your Exeter Reference Number – which can be found on the top of your original offer email). We aim to notify applicants of an outcome within **10 working days**.
Applicants are only permitted to defer entry once. Subsequent to this, a new application will be required which will be considered in line with others applying for entry in that year.
| Start date | Deadline |
| --- | --- |
| Programmes commencing in September | **30 September** |
| All other start dates | **Within 4 weeks of the start date of your programme** |
Applicants who do not request a deferral within this timeframe will be required to reapply, as your original application and documentation will not be retained.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
Your offer will be either **Conditional** or **Unconditional**:
- **Conditional** means that you have not yet satisfied academic, English language or any other entry requirements. Details of offer conditions and how to satisfy these requirements, including [paying your deposit](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/masters-degrees/fees/tuition-fee-deposit/), will be given in the offer letter.
- For a **full-time taught postgraduate programme**, applicants need to pay the deposit to secure their place and should pay by the deadline even if they have not yet met all the conditions of the offer.
- The deadline for meeting all conditions of the offer is normally **31 August** for September entry. Applicants must supply required documentation showing they have met outstanding academic requirements, English language and/or references, or inform the University by **31 August** what conditions are still to be met and when they expect to meet them.
- If the University does not hear from the applicant by **31 August** and outstanding conditions remain, it reserves the right to either withdraw or defer the application to the following year.
- To receive a formal unconditional offer letter and, where needed, a Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies to apply for a Student Visa, applicants must meet academic conditions by providing copies of degree certificates, transcripts and references as explained in the conditional offer letter; non-academic conditions such as a [DBS](http://www.exeter.ac.uk/dbs/) check; and the required standard of English language competence by providing an English language test certificate meeting the University’s [requirements](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/study/englishlanguagerequirements/).
- Offer holders who successfully complete a [Pre-Sessional English course at the University of Exeter International Study Centre](https://www.exeterisc.com/en/courses/pre-sessional-english) and meet the requirements for progression to their chosen degree are not required to undertake an additional IELTS or TOEFL test. The University does not accept pre-sessional courses delivered by other INTO centres or organisations.
